premise: Adult friendship does not happen by accident. It is built from repeated, initiated contact by someone willing to go first every time, for longer than feels fair. That person is going to be you for the next thirty steps.

reps.label: Reached out first
reps.hint: A message, a call, an invitation. You went first.

reps.label: Invited someone to something
reps.hint: With an actual day and time in it.

reps.label: Turned up to something
reps.hint: Especially the one you nearly cancelled.

reps.label: Got no reply, or a no
reps.hint: Happens constantly. It is the cost of going first.

reps.label: Had a real conversation
reps.hint: Past logistics and weather, into an actual life.

principles.title: Somebody has to go first
principles.body: Most adults are lonely and waiting to be invited. If you decide to be the one who initiates, you will build a circle — not because you are more likeable, but because almost nobody else is doing it. It is unfair and it works.

principles.title: Frequency beats intensity
principles.body: Friendship is built by repetition, not by one great night. Someone you see briefly every week will become closer than someone you see brilliantly twice a year. Optimise for a recurring slot, not for a memorable event.

principles.title: Vagueness is where friendships go to die
principles.body: "We should catch up" is a polite way of not meeting. It costs nothing and produces nothing. A day, a time and a place is a different kind of sentence, and it is the entire difference between intention and a friendship.

principles.title: Nobody is keeping score but you
principles.body: You will initiate far more than you are initiated with, especially early. Keeping a tally will poison it. Either you want these people in your life or you do not — and if you do, going first is simply the price, paid without resentment.

principles.title: Depth comes from disclosure
principles.body: Conversation stays shallow until someone risks something. You do not need a confession — one honest sentence about how something actually went is enough to change the register, and the other person almost always follows.

principles.title: Be useful
principles.body: The fastest route from acquaintance to friend is helping with something real: a move, a deadline, a bad week. Turning up when it is inconvenient does more than a year of pleasant company.

principles.title: Build the room
principles.body: Stop waiting for a group to admit you and start convening one. Whoever sends the message owns the table. It is more work and it is the only reliable way to end up at the centre of something.

principles.title: Let some go
principles.body: Not every connection is meant to be maintained, and dragging dead ones along costs the attention live ones need. Ending or fading a friendship on purpose is not a failure of loyalty. It is honest accounting.

missions.do: List five people you would like to know better. Names, not types.
missions.why: Vague social ambition produces nothing. Five specific people produces a plan.

missions.do: Message one of them today with no agenda.
missions.why: No favour, no reason. Just contact, so the next message is not from nowhere.

missions.do: Invite someone to something specific with a day and a time.
missions.why: This is the entire skill. Everything else is a variation of this sentence.

missions.do: Reply properly to the message you have been leaving unanswered.
missions.why: Avoidance is doing more damage to your circle than any rejection has.

missions.do: Turn up to something you would normally skip.
missions.why: You have declined your way into a small life. Reverse one instance today.

missions.do: Learn and use the name of someone you see regularly but have never asked.
missions.why: Months of shared space, no name. Fix it in ten seconds.

missions.do: Put one recurring social thing in your calendar.
missions.why: Frequency is the mechanism. Get a repeating slot rather than a one-off.

missions.do: Ask someone how something specific went. Something they mentioned before.
missions.why: Remembering the detail is the whole move. It says you were actually listening.

missions.do: Contact someone you have not spoken to in over a year.
missions.why: The silence is heavier in your head than in theirs. Almost always.

missions.do: Invite two people who have never met to the same thing.
missions.why: Introducing people makes you the connection rather than a guest.

missions.do: Tell someone something honest about how your week actually went.
missions.why: Not 'fine'. One true sentence changes what the friendship is allowed to be.

missions.do: Ask a question that cannot be answered in three words.
missions.why: Depth is a choice available in most conversations. Take it deliberately.

missions.do: Spend two hours with someone with no activity to hide behind.
missions.why: A walk, a table, nothing on. Talking is the only thing on the agenda.

missions.do: Help someone with something inconvenient.
missions.why: Convenient help is politeness. Inconvenient help is friendship.

missions.do: Say to one person that you value having them around. Plainly.
missions.why: Adults almost never hear this. It is uncomfortable to say and it lands hard.

missions.do: Ask someone for help with something you would normally handle alone.
missions.why: Being needed builds bonds. Refusing help quietly keeps everyone at arm's length.

missions.do: Initiate every day this week, with anyone. Do not wait once.
missions.why: Seven days of going first. Notice how rarely it costs you anything.

missions.do: Tell someone about something you failed at recently.
missions.why: Competence keeps people at a distance. Fallibility is what lets them close.

missions.do: Follow up on a plan that has gone quiet, without resentment.
missions.why: People are disorganised, not uninterested. Chase it once, cheerfully.

missions.do: Sit with someone having a hard time and do not try to fix it.
missions.why: Presence without solutions is harder than advice and worth considerably more.

missions.do: Host something at your place. Three people is enough.
missions.why: Your room, your responsibility, no exit. This is where a circle starts.

missions.do: Start a recurring thing and run it twice.
missions.why: The second time is what turns an event into a fixture. Get to the second one.

missions.do: Bring someone new into an existing group of yours.
missions.why: Widening the circle is a skill and it makes you the person who does it.

missions.do: Have the conversation with the friend something is off with.
missions.why: Unspoken friction ends more friendships than any argument ever has.

missions.do: Show up for someone at an inconvenient time.
missions.why: Two in the morning, the other side of town. This is the whole currency.

missions.do: Tell someone they are one of your closest friends.
missions.why: Say it. Most people go their entire lives assuming rather than knowing.

missions.do: Let a connection go that you have been maintaining out of guilt.
missions.why: Attention is finite. Spend it on the people who are actually in your life.

missions.do: Run your recurring thing again, even if turnout was bad last time.
missions.why: Everything worth having survives one poor turnout. Most people quit there.

missions.do: Count it honestly: initiations sent, times you turned up, real conversations.
missions.why: Reps, not popularity. The reps are the part you control.

missions.do: Convene the group you wished existed when you started this.
missions.why: Thirty steps ago you were waiting to be invited. Now you are the invitation.
